subject: Phalanx Labs — capacity gate check and escalation playbook
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Phalanx Labs — capacity gate check and escalation playbook

Team —

Phalanx (contact: Lena Torres) is in late-stage legal and is asking us to validate a tight production start window: target go-live 2027-01-15 for initial customers, ramp to sustained 2k qps for embeddings/nearline inference by week 4. Key ask: can we guarantee dedicated pool sizing and an operational fallback if primary node class is constrained?

Quick specifics they shared (attached CSV):
- Model: Llama-3 style 70B dense, typical seq len ~512 tokens, peak burst to 4k tokens per request (rare).
- Expected sustained inference need: 2k qps of short queries + 150 r/s of long context generation (batched).
- Target latency SLO: <150ms 95p for gen use-cases; embeddings SLO <50ms 95p.
- Initial committed term: 12 months starting at go-live, with a signed MOA expected by 2027-01-10.

Ask: please run a capacity availability check for US-west and US-east dedicated pools for the window 2027-01-10 through 2027-02-28. Specifically:
1) What nodes (GPUs + pods) would you recommend for the primary dedicated pool to meet SLOs?
2) Can we place a 30-day operational hold on the necessary capacity (non-binding) to avoid it being allocated elsewhere? If so, what internal approvals are required?
3) What fallback(s) do you recommend (quantized 4-bit variant, T4 burst pods, or multi-model routing) that preserve acceptable latency while reducing immediate demand?

I need a short summarised runbook I can share with Lena and procurement by EOD tomorrow (12/31). I attached the MOA draft they sent.

Thanks —
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0125

Attachments: PHX_MOA_v0.9_draft.pdf (application/pdf, 420KB), phalanx_expected_load_estimates.csv (text/csv, 12KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Phalanx Labs — capacity gate check and escalation playbook

On Wed, 30 Dec 2026, Priya Natarajan wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Phalanx is in late-stage legal and is asking us to validate a tight production start window...

Quick read: the numbers are tight but feasible with staged approach. My high-level notes: 

1) Primary sizing (starting pool):
   - Recommend reserving 8x A100 80GB (dense serving) across US-west + US-east (4+4 split) configured as 16 inference pods (split for redundancy). That should cover steady-state 2k qps for embeddings via batching + 150 r/s long-gen with headroom.
   - If they insist on lower latency for gen, we should increase to 10x A100s (adds ~20% cost).

2) Hold mechanics:
   - We can place a 30-day operational hold in our internal capacity manager (flag: "op_hold_phx_4782"). It's non-binding but stops automatic allocation to new spot-like offers. Requires manager approval from Capacity Ops (my sign-off) and Ops Director (Karthik).

3) Fallbacks and mitigations:
   - Prepare a 4-bit quantized variant of the model as a cold-fallback (saves ~40-60% GPU memory allowing T4-class substitution).
   - Implement prefix/KV cache for repeated traffic patterns to reduce effective compute.
   - Configure multi-tier routing: primary A100 pool, secondary burst T4 pool (lower per-token performance but can absorb sudden spikes).

I'll run a capacity snapshot and node-level availability check by EOD today and include a quick econ estimate. 

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: preliminary_capacity_snapshot-20261230.xlsx (stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 31 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Phalanx Labs — capacity gate check and escalation playbook

Ben / Priya —

Thanks Ben, that aligns with my expectation. A couple of operational notes to include in the runbook for the customer: 

- Approval Path: Ben to create op_hold flag, Karthik to approve (capacity director), and Finance to acknowledge expected committed monthly spend before we convert to reserved capacity. If PO arrives before 30 days expire we can convert hold to dedicated reservation.

- Fallback SLAs: Document that fallback to quantized variant will incur a 10-25% quality delta for generation (we should include a brief note that we can run an eval against their prompt set). Also note that fallback to T4 burst will increase 95p latency by ~2x for gen workloads; acceptable for non-interactive batch inference but not for interactive customers.

- Cross-region smoothing: propose active-active routing with weight 70/30 (us-west primary) and automatic failover to east if we detect sustained load >85% capacity or node failures.

Action items for sales (Priya):
- Get written expected go-live date and signed MOA or PO by 2027-01-10.
- Share a 3-5 prompt eval set for quality validation on quantized variant.

I'll approve the op_hold once Ben creates the snapshot and the finance estimate is in.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Capacity & Infrastructure Operations
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

> On Wed, 30 Dec 2026 10:04, Ben Carter wrote:
> > I'll run a capacity snapshot and node-level availability check by EOD today and include a quick econ estimate.

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Torres <lena.torres@phalanxlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@phalanxlabs.com
Date: Sun, 03 Jan 2027 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Phalanx Labs — capacity gate check and escalation playbook (summary)

Lena / Phalanx procurement —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the MOA draft. Quick summary of our internal findings and next steps from Redwood: 

Summary:
- Primary recommendation: 8x A100 80GB (4x US-west, 4x US-east) as an initial dedicated pool to meet your stated SLOs. We can scale to 10x if you finalize lower latency requirements for generation.
- Operational hold: Redwood can place a 30-day operational hold on the proposed capacity to protect against allocation while you finalize legal/PO. This hold is non-binding and requires approval from Redwood Capacity Director. We will notify you when the hold is active.
- Fallbacks: We propose a quantized 4-bit model variant plus a secondary T4 burst pool for absorbable spikes. Note that T4 fallback will not meet interactive gen latency goals — it is intended for batch/backfill use.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm expected go-live date and share a signed MOA or tentative PO by 2027-01-10 so we can convert the hold to a reservation.
2) Share a 3–5 prompt eval set to validate quantized-model quality (send to priya.natarajan@redwood.ai).
3) Procurement: once we have a PO, Redwood Finance will issue an invoice schedule and Ben will convert the hold to a formal reservation.

I'll enable the internal op_hold flag once I receive confirmation of the go-live date from you. If anything changes, ping me and I'll escalate with Karthik.

Best —
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0125

---
Priya's internal note (not for procurement): Ben's snapshot shows 6x A100 absolutely available and 2x coming free in ~10 days from a scheduled decommission — I'll ask for the 30-day hold to be created ASAP so procurement has breathing room.
